41#' Gate a flow run and quantify the knock-in fraction
42#' @param fcs path to an .fcs file
43#' @param gates a gate definition, see gates.yaml
44
45quantify_ki <- function(fcs, gates, min_events = 10000) {
46 ff <- flowCore::read.FCS(fcs, transformation = FALSE)
47 stopifnot(nrow(ff) >= min_events)
48
49 # singlets first — order matters, see issue #40
50 live <- apply_gate(ff, gates$singlets) |>
51 apply_gate(gates$viable)
52
53 gfp <- apply_gate(live, gates$gfp_pos)
54 mch <- apply_gate(live, gates$mcherry_pos)
55
56 list(
57 efficiency = nrow(gfp) / nrow(live) * 100,
58 n_live = nrow(live),
59 gate_hash = digest(gates)
60 )
61}
README.md
gate-and-quantify — the gating pipeline behind DS-1174 and MC-0288. Reads an FCS file and a YAML gate definition, returns efficiency, live count and a hash of the gates used, so a number can always be traced to the gate that produced it.

OUTPUTS ARE DIFFED TOO
A notebook diff that only shows source changes hides the thing that matters — R² moved from 0.41 to 0.89 and the figure changed shape. Both are rendered side by side.
CELL ORDER IS RECORDED
Execution counts are part of the diff. A notebook whose cells ran out of order is flagged, because that is the single most common source of an irreproducible figure.

THE FIGURE DID NOT MATCH BYTE FOR BYTE
Font rendering differs between machines. The underlying plotted values are identical, so the badge holds — but the mismatch is shown rather than swallowed, because a checker that quietly ignores differences is not a checker.
WHEN IT IS LOST
The badge is suspended automatically if a merge changes any output, if the pinned base image disappears, or if the re-run has not succeeded in 12 months. It is a current fact, not a historical award.

THE CAP IS THE POINT
J-4463 was stopped at four times its estimate, having produced a partial checkpoint that was kept. A runaway GPU job on a fixed-budget grant is a real harm, and the default is to stop and ask rather than to finish and invoice.
WHO APPROVES WHAT
Under €5, anyone in the project. Over €5, the PI is asked once with the estimate and the reason. The threshold is set by the institution, not by us.

PROJECTION
At the current rate the compute allocation runs out in 14 months, three months before the grant ends. The segmentation work is 76% of it — worth a conversation before it becomes an emergency.
WHERE JOBS RUN
VSC Tier-2 · institutionalconnected
Managed cloud · EU-westconnected
SLURM at Karolinskavia collaborator
The same launch spec runs on any of them. Where a job lands is a scheduling and cost decision, not a rewrite.
Every job records the code version, the data version and the environment digest — so a number in a paper can be traced to the exact job that produced it, and that job can be run again.
